solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Italian writer's snake constricting 200 with one more loop

definitions.note: possessive in the clue; the 's links definition to wordplay

indicators.note: a constricting snake wraps itself around its prey, so these letters go round the next ones

parts.note: the boa is a constrictor snake
200 in Roman numerals
200 with one more is 201, CCI in Roman numerals
a loop is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A writer from Italy is said to own a snake that wraps around things with one loop too many.
explanation.walkthrough: The 200 does double duty: once inside the snake, and again as the base of 201. Roman numerals are a standard crossword source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Boccaccio, author of the Decameron, was a fourteenth-century Italian storyteller and poet.

clue.text: Black space in print goes round like this sweep

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: something that goes round encircles, so the printer's space surrounds the next word

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
'so' means in this way

explanation.surface: A printer notes a dark gap on the page and how it curls round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black space in print' reads as one idea, an inked gap, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom of twigs, and to besom is to clean a floor with one, Scots and dialect usage.

clue.text: Brubeck's Back in Black? Using their first names is a source of poison

indicators.note: the reversed name goes inside the singer's name

parts.note: the singer Cilla Black, by her first name, as the clue says both people are named this way

indicators.note: back means the pianist's first name is read in reverse

parts.note: the jazz pianist Dave Brubeck, by his first name

explanation.surface: A quiz about a jazz pianist covering the AC/DC song Back in Black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in Black' looks like the AC/DC album title; the question mark and 'Using their first names' tell you to swap each surname for its owner's first name. Cilla Black was a British singer and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cevadilla, also sabadilla, is a Mexican plant whose seeds yield veratrine, a toxic alkaloid.

clue.text: Edible seed cooked in a bake contains depleted uranium

indicators.note: contains says the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation inside them
cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
DU is the standard abbreviation for depleted uranium

explanation.surface: A recipe note: an edible seed cooked in a bake turns out to contain depleted uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked in' reads as one phrase, but 'in' belongs to the letters being rearranged; DU then sits after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: The aduki is a small red bean from an Asian plant, eaten whole or made into sweet paste.

clue.text: Conservative Muslim's allowed to hold minor worker and charge Roman for this, relating to engravings

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the permitted-food word surrounds what follows

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
halal means permitted under Islamic law
a cog in the machine is a minor worker
a rap is a criminal charge
hic is Latin for 'this'

explanation.surface: A tale of a Tory, a Muslim's permitted food, a lowly worker, a criminal charge and a Roman, all somehow about engraving.
explanation.walkthrough: C, then HALAL holding COG, RAP and HIC: C + HAL(COG RAP HIC)AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalcography is the art of engraving on copper or brass, so the adjective describes that craft.

clue.text: With jaws that recede as though potion's foul

indicators.note: something foul has gone bad, so the letters before it are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: all fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drinker grimaces with a receding jaw, as though the potion tasted foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Opisthognathous is a zoological term for having retreating jaws, from Greek for 'behind' and 'jaw'.

clue.text: Pleasant, not too warm, with temperature set to 50

indicators.note: the temperature letter is set to a new value, i.e. swapped for fifty

parts.note: tepid means lukewarm, only slightly warm
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A mild day with the thermostat set to fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: In TEPID, 'set to' changes the T into L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepid is a rare old word for pleasant or charming, from Latin lepidus.

clue.text: Flat area turned off none, presumably

indicators.note: turned means read from the other end, as a down entry is read upward

parts.note: each word swapped for its opposite: off becomes on, none becomes all; 'presumably' admits the trick

explanation.surface: A flat area where someone turned off nothing, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposite of 'off none' is ON ALL, which turned gives LLANO.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a vast grassy plain of South America, especially in Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: What's standard to protect head in Goa, India?

definitions.text: What's standard to protect head in Goa, India?

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the standard goes round a letter

parts.note: par is the standard score

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from the place name

parts.note: the start of the Indian state's name
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Asking what is normally worn to protect the head in Goa or elsewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR protecting G, then I: PA(G)R + I. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagri is the turban commonly worn by men in India, a standard covering that shields the head.

clue.text: Weasel cat (northern, mouse-coloured) seen in swamp mostly

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so the bracketed pieces go into the swamp
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to swamp is to deluge
N is the abbreviation for northern
dun is a dull greyish-brown

explanation.surface: A naturalist describes a weasel-like cat, northern and mouse-grey, glimpsed in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swamp' looks like a noun for the animal's habitat; it is the verb, meaning flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The delundung is the banded linsang, a small slender carnivore of Southeast Asia related to civets.

clue.text: Queen Victoria in fits over caviar

indicators.note: 'in' places the royal cipher inside the word for fits
turned over means the word for fits is read backwards

parts.note: agues are fits of shivering fever
VR, Victoria Regina, was her royal cipher

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria throws a tantrum over the caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fits' looks like a royal temper; fits here are bouts of feverish shivering.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevruga is caviar from the sevruga sturgeon of the Caspian and Black Seas.

clue.text: Nasty bugs ail plantain seeds

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of shape, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Nasty insects are attacking the plantain seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabgul, or ispaghula, is the husk of a plantain species used as a laxative fibre.

clue.text: What's pretentious for me, former princess wears divine headdresses

indicators.note: whoever wears something has it on, so the affected word goes round the princess

parts.note: the French word used affectedly in English for 'me'
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A posh speaker says 'moi' while the late princess sports divine headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: Read normally, the princess wears the hats; cryptically, the affected 'me' wears her.
explanation.definitionFit: A modius is the cylindrical crown worn by certain gods such as Serapis in classical art; modii is its plural.

clue.text: Move an inch, even if entering like a ghost

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the short word goes into the rearranged letters
moving things changes their positions, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
tho' is a short form of 'though', meaning even if

explanation.surface: Advice to creep forward an inch at a time, even when going in, like a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Chthonian means dwelling in the underworld, the realm of the dead and of spirits.

clue.text: This girl Vera would return a wake-up call

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the phrase is read from its end

parts.note: reveille is the bugle call that wakes soldiers
taken as written; this name is set aside at the end

explanation.surface: A girl and Vera bounce a wake-up call back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer followed by VERA, read backwards, spells A REVEILLE. Remove VERA and ELLIE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellie is a girl's given name, so 'this girl' points to a name for the answer.

clue.text: Savour of burning page raised doubt without question in novel

indicators.note: 'in' sets the earlier pieces inside the title of the book

parts.note: Emma, Jane Austen's novel
P is the abbreviation for page

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means written from the bottom up
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the word for doubt

parts.note: a query is a doubt raised
Q is the abbreviation for question; it is removed

explanation.surface: A reader smells burning; a page raises an unanswered doubt in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' applies to the shortened doubt only, not the page; the novel is Jane Austen's, a frequent crossword container.
explanation.definitionFit: Empyreuma is the acrid taste or smell of organic matter that has been charred.

clue.text: Sentimentality put on at an early age — no good leaving congratulations

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the abbreviated letters come out of the word for youthful

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality
to don clothes is to put them on
young means at an early age
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Gushing about someone's early talent, then losing the good bits before offering praise.
explanation.walkthrough: GOO + DON + YOUNG minus NG.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Good on you' is an informal phrase of praise or approval, especially in Australian and British speech.

clue.text: Pompous nonsense accepted in Ring Cycle

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

indicators.note: something accepted in is let inside, so the nonsense word goes into the cycle

parts.note: a round is a cycle
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A critic calls Wagner's Ring Cycle pompous nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring Cycle' looks like Wagner's four operas, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ororotund is a jocular extension of orotund, meaning bombastic or grandiloquent in speech.

clue.text: Still eating in the way that is even more barmy than the rest

definitions.text: even more barmy than the rest

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the word for still holds the next pieces

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
a as in 'twice a day', meaning per or in
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
i.e. stands for 'that is', with the contracted 's of 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone still at the table seems madder than everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Barm is the froth on fermenting beer, so barmy literally means frothy with ferment as well as crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy literally means covered in barm, the froth of fermenting liquor, so the most barmy thing is the most frothy with that ferment.

clue.text: Note penned by Greek poet, note simply to fill a gap?

indicators.note: something penned by a writer is enclosed by him, so the poet's name goes round the note

parts.note: Pindar, the lyric poet of ancient Greece
la, the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A note written by an ancient Greek poet, perhaps just to fill a gap on the page.
explanation.walkthrough: P(LA)INDAR + N. The question mark flags that the gap is a hole in fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: To plain-darn is to mend a hole in cloth with ordinary straightforward darning stitches.

clue.text: Old gold coin with none of the buck's spending power?

parts.note: O is zero, none
from the idiom 'bang for your buck', meaning value for money

explanation.surface: An old gold coin worth nothing compared with what a dollar can buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' is US slang for a dollar, and 'bang for the buck' is what your money gets you.
explanation.definitionFit: The obang was a large oval gold coin issued in feudal Japan, now an antique.

clue.text: Act of sniper possibly trapping people in rampage

indicators.note: trapping something holds it inside, so the word for rampage goes round the people

parts.note: a riot is a violent rampage
flesh as in 'all flesh', humankind

explanation.surface: A sniper's attack catches people caught up in a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: RI(FLESH)OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper fires from a rifle, so a single discharge is one example of what a sniper does.

clue.text: Foreign Office pardon, conclusion of politician's hot air in high places

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
'eh?' asks someone to repeat, like 'pardon?'

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the end of the word politician

explanation.surface: A diplomat's pardon is mocked as so much hot air among the powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot air in high places' sounds like bluster from the powerful; it is a mountain wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The foehn is a warm dry wind blowing down the lee slopes of mountains such as the Alps.

clue.text: Spenser's simply uncivilised when unconfined

definitions.note: an old word used by the poet Spenser meaning easily or simply

indicators.note: with its confining outer letters removed, only the inside of the word is left

parts.note: heathen can mean barbarous or uncivilised

explanation.surface: A literary critic calling the Elizabethan poet's language plain and barbaric once set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when unconfined' strips the H and N from the ends of HEATHEN. Spenser's archaic spellings are standard in advanced puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Eathe is an archaic adverb, found in Spenser, meaning easily, without difficulty.

clue.text: Time in pub bar first using smaller base than usual

indicators.note: 'in' places the time abbreviation inside the shortened pub word
bar means except, so the opening letter is excluded

parts.note: one's local is one's regular pub
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Drinking time in the pub bar, first going with a cheaper base than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub counter but means except: LOCAL minus L, with T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal counting works in base eight, a smaller radix than the familiar decimal base ten.

clue.text: Indisposed, clutching a metal pot

indicators.note: clutching holds something tight inside, so the word for reluctant surrounds a letter

parts.note: loth means reluctant, disinclined
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone feeling unwell clings to a metal pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indisposed' suggests illness, but here it means unwilling: LOT(A)H.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotah is a small round brass or copper water vessel used in India.

clue.text: Most of large towns see university's backing of complaint affecting vision

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the whole string is read from its end
most of means not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: cities are large towns
v. stands for vide, Latin for see
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university study of an eye complaint common in big towns.
explanation.walkthrough: CITIE + V + U, all reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea, the eye's middle layer, and uveitic is its adjective.

clue.text: Rich, not poor, about to whine

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the whining word
poor here means badly made, so the letters of not are put out of order

parts.note: to pule is to whimper or whine

explanation.surface: A wealthy person, not hard up, about to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not poor' reads as a phrase meaning rich, but 'poor' rearranges NOT into ONT, which goes 'about' PULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent means lavishly wealthy or luxurious.

clue.text: Female senior apprentice dumping duo in the van

indicators.note: the van is the front, so a pair of letters at the start is thrown away

parts.note: an apprentice is a trainee

explanation.surface: A senior woman takes on an apprentice who dumps a couple of things in the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' suggests a vehicle; here it is the vanguard, the front. TRAINEE loses TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ainée is French for elder, the feminine form, used after a woman's name to mark the older sister.

clue.text: Desperate youth crossing street before long

indicators.note: crossing over something spans it, so the boy's word straddles the road abbreviation

parts.note: a lad is a youth
St is the abbreviation for street
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A desperate teenager dashes across the road before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before long' looks like the phrase meaning soon; 'before' just places one piece ahead of the other, and 'long' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final attempt made in extremity, when all else has failed.
